title: Await work and honor cancellation
summary: Convert a blocking count into an async method that observes a cancellation token.

scenario.briefing: A reporting endpoint counts large batches. The current method blocks with .Result and ignores cancellation, so a canceled request keeps working. Make the method async and cooperative.

objectives.description: Await asynchronous work instead of blocking.
Explain tasks, cancellation, and async void accurately.

hints: An async method returns Task<int>, not int.
Await each unit of work instead of reading .Result.
Pass the token to Task.Delay and check it before the work.

misconceptions.testDescription: The method awaits instead of blocking.
misconceptions.feedback: Await the task so the calling thread is released. .Result blocks and can deadlock in a synchronization context.

misconceptions.description: Returning async void from a library method.
misconceptions.feedback: A library method should return Task so callers can await completion and observe exceptions.

misconceptions.description: Believing async void methods can be awaited.
misconceptions.feedback: async void has no awaitable handle. Use async Task for anything a caller needs to observe.

sections.title: Async work is awaited, not blocked
sections.body: An async method returns a Task that represents work in progress. await releases the current thread until the task completes. Calling .Result or .Wait blocks the thread and can deadlock when a synchronization context is involved.

sections.title: Cancellation is cooperative
sections.body: A CancellationToken is passed into asynchronous work. The work checks ThrowIfCancellationRequested or passes the token to APIs that observe it. Cancellation is a request, not an interruption, so every long-running operation must cooperate.

sections.title: Async all the way down
sections.body: Return Task or Task<T> from asynchronous methods so callers can await them. async void is appropriate only for top-level event handlers because the caller cannot observe completion or exceptions.

quiz.explanation: Task<Report> lets the caller await completion, and the token lets it cancel. async void hides completion, while a synchronous method blocks the caller.

steps.explanation: await keeps the caller responsive, cancellation is a request, and Task.WhenAll composes independent work. async void cannot be awaited.
